Implement slugify per the docstring:
- Lowercase ASCII; accented Latin characters reduced to base letters (é -> e) → use unicodedata.normalize('NFKD') or NFD, encode to ascii ignore, or NFKD and drop combining marks.
- All runs of non a-z/0-9 → single "-"
- No leading/trailing "-"
- Truncate to max_len chars, never end in "-"
- Empty result → "untitled"

Implementation:

```python
import re
import unicodedata


def slugify(title, max_len=50):
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title)
    text = "".join(ch for ch in text if not unicodedata.combining(ch))
    text = text.lower()
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text)
    text = text.strip("-")[:max_len].rstrip("-")
    return text or "untitled"
```

Wait: NFKD can also reduce other characters (e.g. ﬁ ligature → fi, superscripts). The docstring says "accented Latin letters reduced to base letters (é -> e)". NFKD is fine and common. Note however that NFKD may decompose some non-Latin characters too (e.g. ㈪, superscripts). Fine.

Order matters: lowercasing before or after normalization? NFKD then lower, or lower then NFKD — for these characters the result is equivalent. "É".lower() = "é", then NFKD gives "e". Fine.

Truncation edge case: truncate to max_len, then rstrip("-"). If the title is all non-alphanumeric, text becomes all dashes, strip("-") yields "" → "untitled". Good.

Edge case: what if truncation leaves only dashes? e.g. title "a" + 60 chars... "a" + "-"*60: text = "a-"*... after strip = "a-" * n, truncated to 50 chars could be "a-a-..." ending with "-", rstrip handles that. What if truncation lands right on a dash? e.g. "abc-" * 20, 50 chars = "abc-" *12 + "ab", ends with "b", fine. What about "a" + "-" * 100: strip → "a" + "-"*100, [:50] = "a" + "-"*49 → rstrip → "a". Fine.

Edge case: what if truncation result is entirely dashes? e.g. "a" + "b" ... hard to get all-dashes after strip. "ab-cd": fine. If max_len truncation splits a run of dashes at the end? e.g. "a" + "-"*60: [:50] = "a" + "-"*49, rstrip → "a". OK.

What if result after truncation is all dashes, e.g. title = "-"*10? strip → "" → "untitled". Good.

Write it, run the test.

import re
import unicodedata


def slugify(title, max_len=50):
    """Turn a title into a URL slug.

    - lowercase ASCII; accented Latin letters are reduced to their base letter (é -> e)
    - every run of characters that are not a-z or 0-9 becomes a single "-"
    - no leading or trailing "-"
    - truncated to at most max_len characters, never ending in "-"
    - an empty result becomes "untitled"
    """
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title)
    text = "".join(ch for ch in text if not unicodedata.combining(ch))
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text.lower())
    text = text.strip("-")[:max_len].rstrip("-")
    return text or "untitled"

    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title)
    text = "".join(ch for ch in text if not unicodedata.combining(ch))
    text = text.lower()
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text)
    text = text.strip("-")[:max_len].rstrip("-")
    return text or "untitled"

What if result after truncation is all dashes, e.g. title = "-"*10? strip → "" → "untitled". Good.

import re
import unicodedata


def slugify(title, max_len=50):
    """Turn a title into a URL slug.

    - lowercase ASCII; accented Latin letters are reduced to their base letter (é -> e)
    - every run of characters that are not a-z or 0-9 becomes a single "-"
    - no leading or trailing "-"
    - truncated to at most max_len characters, never ending in "-"
    - an empty result becomes "untitled"
    """
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title)
    text = "".join(ch for ch in text if not unicodedata.combining(ch))
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text.lower())
    text = text.strip("-")[:max_len].rstrip("-")
    return text or "untitled"

NFKD decomposition: é → e + combining acute; stripping the combining character leaves e. Also, NFKD decomposes superscript/ligatures too, so it's a bonus. However, note: NFKD also converts, for example, "㈪" into "K", or Roman numerals into letters — within acceptable range.

One issue: the docstring says "lowercase ASCII" — what about non-ASCII characters that can't be decomposed (e.g., CJK)? They're not included in a-z0-9 → they become "-", which matches "all consecutive non-a-z/0-9 characters become a single -".

- empty result → `"untitled"`
